exercise.name: Cable High Row
aliases: High cable row to the chest

reference.title: Cable High Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (shoulder horizontal abduction and extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row the bar to the upper chest, breathe in as the arms reach back toward the pulley.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s pull, short squeeze, about 2 s return

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can row to the upper chest with the elbows high and no shrug.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; add a 1 s squeeze

cues.text: Sit tall on the seat facing a pulley set above head height, feet flat; hold the bar overhand, wider than the shoulders, arms long and reaching up toward the pulley.
Breathe out; draw the shoulder blades together and row the bar to the upper chest, elbows high and out to the sides.
Bar just below the collarbones, elbows about shoulder height and slightly behind the trunk, shoulders down.
Breathe in and let the arms reach back up toward the pulley under control.
Brief stretch with the arms long, then row again.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the elbows into a low row
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about shoulder height and the bar at the upper chest.
Pull the shoulder blades back and down; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back to move the weight
mistakes.fix: Sit tall and keep the trunk still.
Keep the wrists straight in line with the forearms.

kinematics.norm: Elbows about shoulder height at the finish (clinical opinion); horizontal abduction with the arm raised works the posterior deltoid (Schoenfeld 2013)
From nearly straight to about 90-120 degrees (clinical opinion)
Protracted with the arms long, retracted at the finish; retraction drives the middle trapezius and rhomboids (Oyama 2010)
Overhand, wider than the shoulders (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s pull and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable High Row, video (movement reference)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain at the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can row with the shoulders down and the trunk still.
Keep the cable in front of the face: sit far enough back that the bar does not pass close to the head.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort with high elbows: lower the elbows a little toward a mid-height row (clinical opinion).
Wrist discomfort with the straight bar: use a rope with a neutral grip.

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blade back toward the spine.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blade back toward the spine.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: pulls the raised arm back (horizontal abduction).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: pulls the raised arm back (horizontal abduction).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Helps pull the arm down and back from the reach.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Helps pull the arm down and back from the reach.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Bends the elbow as the bar comes in.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Bends the elbow as the bar comes in.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Steadies the shoulder and helps pull the arm back.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Steadies the shoulder and helps pull the arm back.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder girdle with the arms raised; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder girdle with the arms raised; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk still on the seat.

guides.label: Bar to the upper chest, elbows high
Elbows well bent at the finish
